info.title: Xenon API
info.description:
The REST API of a Xenon server: the devices in your lab, the Appium sessions that run on them, live device control, recordings, selector health and administration. The dashboard uses this same API.

This reference describes version **__XENON_VERSION__**. Every path below is relative to `/xenon`, so `/api/devices` is `https://<your-xenon-host>/xenon/api/devices`. The raw OpenAPI document is at `/xenon/api-docs.json` on your server.

## Authentication

Every endpoint needs a credential, except the few marked as public (health checks, sign-in, password reset and the JWKS). The four ways to authenticate are:

| Credential | How to send it | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| **Access key and API token** | `x-xenon-access-key` and `x-xenon-token` headers | Scripts, CI, SDKs, a node reporting to its hub |
| **Bearer token** | `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` | Short-lived access; mint one with `POST /api/auth/token` (audience `xenon-rest`, 1 hour) |
| **Dashboard session** | `xenon_dashboard_session` cookie, set by `POST /api/auth/login` | The browser dashboard |
| **Hub token** | `x-xenon-hub-token` header | Hub to node only; Xenon sends it itself |

Find your access key and create API tokens on your profile page (`/xenon/profile`, **API tokens**).

**Scopes.** An API token carries scopes: `read`, `sessions`, `devices` and `admin`. `admin` satisfies any scope. A signed-in dashboard user gets the scopes of their role: members have `devices`, `sessions` and `read`; admins also have `admin`. A request without the scope it needs gets `403`.

**Roles.** Some endpoints also need a role: `MEMBER`, `ADMIN` or `SUPER_ADMIN`. Each says so in its description.

**Teams.** A member sees only their teams' devices and the shared pool, and the sessions, apps and selectors that go with them. Something outside your teams answers exactly as if it didn't exist: `404`.

**Same-origin check.** A state-changing request (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) must carry an `Origin` or `Referer` header from the same host as the server, or it gets `403`. Requests sent with the access key and token headers, an `Authorization: Bearer` token, or a hub token are exempt: a browser can't send those headers from another site. So only a script that calls a public endpoint such as `POST /api/auth/login` needs to send an `Origin` header.

## Errors

Errors are JSON with an `error` field. An unexpected server error is `500` with `{ "error": "internal", "message": "Internal server error" }`; the details go to the server's log. Newer endpoints put a stable, machine-readable code there (`not_found`, `device_held_by_another_user`) with a human-readable `message`. Older ones put the message itself in `error`, or `true` with a `message`. Branch on the HTTP status first.

## Rate limits

Every request with a credential is rate limited, except single-use tickets. An access key has its own budgets; a signed-in user's dashboard sessions and bearer tokens share one set of budgets per user (300 a minute). Each has three request budgets, refilled every minute:
- `read`: GET requests (ten times the budget for a signed-in user or a bearer token, since a dashboard page loads many images at once);
- `heavy`: AI, healing and visual endpoints (a quarter of the budget, at least 10);
- `control`: everything else.

Each such response carries `X-RateLimit-Category`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Capacity`. Past the budget the answer is `429` with `Retry-After` in seconds.

## Appium sessions

Appium's WebDriver API (`POST /session` and the session's commands, under Appium's own base path) is not part of this reference. A session authenticates in its capabilities, under `xe:options`, with one of:
- `accessKey` and `token`;
- `sessionToken`, minted by `POST /api/auth/token`.

Either names the session's owner only while that user exists and is active, and a session token needs the `sessions` scope, as a key does. A key or token that doesn't check out counts as none: with `XENON_REQUIRE_SESSION_TOKEN` the session is refused, without it the session runs with no owner.

A leased device also takes `leaseId` and `leaseToken`, which the lease's `appiumCapabilities` already carry. Xenon removes these credentials before the driver or any stored record sees them.

## Live streams

Device previews and live logs use WebSockets, outside this reference:
- `/xenon/api/control/{udid}/stream/h264`
- `/xenon/api/control/{udid}/logcat`

Both are opened with a ticket from `POST /api/control/{udid}/stream/ticket`. Socket.IO at `/socket.io/` carries the dashboard's live events.

post.summary: Tap the screen
post.description:
Taps the device screen once at (`x`, `y`), in the device's screen points (the `screenWidth` × `screenHeight` the device list reports). Android taps through `adb shell input tap`; iOS through WebDriverAgent.

Needs the `MEMBER` role and the `devices` scope. Refused with `409` while another user holds the device (their live preview or recording) or runs an Appium session on it; admins are exempt, and your own Appium session on it stays controllable.

On a hub, for a node's phone, the request is sent on to that node once (never retried), signed for you, and the node's answer is relayed unchanged. A cloud provider's phone answers `501`.

get.description:
Says whether the device's preview is running and which transport a player should use (`type`: `h264` on Android when the server's `streaming.androidH264` setting is on and the device isn't being recorded, else `mjpeg`). A device with no preview answers `200` with `status: stopped`. iOS adds WebDriverAgent's port, the start time and the last error.

Open to watchers. Needs the `MEMBER` role; any scope will do.

On a hub, for a node's phone, the request is sent on to that node once (never retried), signed for you, and the node's answer is relayed unchanged. A cloud provider's phone answers `501`.

post.summary: Stop watching the preview
post.description:
Tells the server a page stopped watching (navigated away, closed, reloaded). Nothing stops at once: after a 3-second grace the preview is stopped and your hold released only if nobody is watching it and no recording reads it. A `stream/start` within the grace (a reload) cancels it. Use this rather than `stream/stop` when other tabs may be watching.

You may leave a device you hold, one with a legacy hold, or any device as an admin; another user's hold answers `403`.

Needs the `MEMBER` role and the `devices` scope.

On a hub, for a node's phone, the request is sent on to that node once (never retried), signed for you, and the node's answer is relayed unchanged. A cloud provider's phone answers `501`.

post.summary: Stop the preview and release the device
post.description:
Stops the device's preview on every transport at once and releases its preview hold, including a hold left over from a restart. Every other tab watching the device loses its preview too; prefer `stream/leave`. On iOS the stream is kept while an Appium session on the phone may be using its WebDriverAgent.

You may stop a device you hold, one with a legacy hold, or (as an admin) any device, which force-releases another user's hold. Refused with `409 device_recording` while the device is being recorded: stop the recording instead (`POST /api/recordings/{groupId}/stop`).

Needs the `MEMBER` role and the `devices` scope.

On a hub, for a node's phone, the request is sent on to that node once (never retried), signed for you, and the node's answer is relayed unchanged. A cloud provider's phone answers `501`. The hub also refuses with `409 device_recording` while it records the node's phone.

get.summary: List the devices in the lab
get.description:
Every device this server knows: its own phones and, on a hub, the
phones its nodes report. Each row carries `teamName`, the name of
its team (null for the shared pool).

Needs role `MEMBER` or above; no scope is checked. A member sees the
shared pool and their teams' devices only. An admin, or any caller
on a server with auth disabled, sees every device.

With `sessionId`, the answer is the one visible device whose
`session_id` is that value, as an object, or an empty `200` body
when there is none. When the Appium dashboard plugin is installed,
each row in the list also gets `dashboard_link` and
`total_session_count`. Xenon reaches the plugin on this server's own
address and port, and the link is `<XENON_PUBLIC_URL>/dashboard?…`,
or `/dashboard?…` on the server the caller has open when
`XENON_PUBLIC_URL` isn't set. Through 2.14 both were built from the
`Host` header of the first request after startup, signed in or not.

`GET /api/device` is the same endpoint.

get.summary: List the devices in the lab (alias)
get.description:
The same as `GET /api/devices`: every device the caller may see,
with `teamName`, or with `sessionId` the one device running that
session. Needs role `MEMBER` or above. A member sees the shared pool
and their teams' devices only.

get.summary: List the devices of one platform
get.description:
The devices of one platform, filtered like `GET /api/devices`: a
member sees the shared pool and their teams' devices only. Each row
carries `teamName`. Needs role `MEMBER` or above.

`platform` is matched case-insensitively. Any other value than
`ios` or `android` answers `200` with an empty list, not an error.
`booted` keeps only devices whose `state` is `Booted` (simulators):
any value turns it on, `booted=false` included.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: The platform, `ios` or `android` (any letter case).

parameters.name: deviceType
parameters.description: Keep only devices of this type.

parameters.name: booted
parameters.description: Present (with any value) to keep only devices whose `state` is `Booted`.

200.description: The matching devices; empty for an unknown platform.

post.summary: Block a device for maintenance
post.description:
Sets `userBlocked` on a device, so no new session or lease is
allocated to it. A session already running on it is not affected,
and neither is `busy`. The device stays blocked when it disconnects
and comes back, through restarts too.

Send both `udid` and `host`, exactly as `GET /api/devices` shows
them: the device is the row of that udid on that host. Without
either, `400`; with no such row, `404`. Through 2.12 the body was a
device filter, so an empty body blocked the first device in the
list, and a udid alone either row of a udid two nodes report
(emulators).

Needs role `ADMIN` and the `devices` scope.

500.description: The device could not be updated.

post.summary: Unblock a device
post.description:
Clears `userBlocked`, so the device can be allocated again. Send
both `udid` and `host`, as for `POST /api/block`: without either,
`400`; with no such row, `404`.

Needs role `ADMIN` and the `devices` scope.

500.description: The device could not be updated.

post.summary: Replace a device's tags
post.description:
Replaces the device's tag list with `tags` (it doesn't append). Tags
are free-form labels, such as `flaky` or `lab-row-3`, that a lease
can filter on. The row is chosen by exact `udid` and `host`; a pair
that names no device is `404` (through 2.13 it changed nothing and
answered `200`). The device keeps its tags when it disconnects and
comes back, through restarts too.

Needs role `ADMIN` and the `devices` scope.

host.description: The device's host, exactly as `GET /api/devices` shows it.

400.description: `udid` or `host` is missing, or `tags` is not an array.

example.error: Missing udid, host, or tags array

404.description: No device of that udid on that host.

put.summary: Assign a device to a team
put.description:
Gives the device to a team, or with `teamId: null` returns it to the
shared pool, which every member sees. A missing `teamId` counts as
null. Every device with this udid changes (on a hub, each node that
reports it), and allocation and live dashboard events follow the new
team at once.

A device keeps its team when it disconnects and comes back, through
restarts too, and this also moves one of this udid that isn't
connected now: a team that one belongs to can't be deleted.

Needs role `ADMIN` and the `admin` scope.

parameters.name: udid
parameters.description: The device's udid.

teamId.description: The team's id, or null for the shared pool.

200.description: The device's team changed. `updated` is how many devices changed, connected or not.

404.description: The team or the device doesn't exist.

get.summary: List the current reservations
get.description:
The devices reserved right now (an expired reservation isn't
listed), with the time left. A member sees only reservations on the
shared pool and their teams' devices; an admin sees all.

Needs role `MEMBER` or above. Reservations are deprecated in favour
of leases (`POST /api/sdk/leases`): every answer carries
`Deprecation`, `Sunset` and `Link` headers.

post.summary: Reserve a device
post.description:
Marks a device as reserved by `reservedBy` until now plus
`duration`. `reservedBy` is the name shown on the device; the
reservation also records the signed-in user who took it
(`reservedByUserId`), who alone, or an admin, may release or extend
it. A device already reserved by someone else, or running an Appium
session, is refused with `409`. The same user under the same
`reservedBy` may reserve it again, which restarts the clock. The
reservation lasts until it ends even if the device disconnects or
the server restarts meanwhile; one that ended while the device was
away is not brought back.

The device is the row of `udid` on `host`, so send both exactly as
`GET /api/devices` shows them. No such row, or a device outside the
caller's teams, answers `404`, as an unknown one.

Needs role `MEMBER` or above and the `devices` scope. Deprecated in
favour of leases: every answer carries `Deprecation`, `Sunset` and
`Link` headers.

reservedBy.description: Who the reservation is for, as free text.

400.description: A field is missing, or `duration` is invalid or outside 1 minute to 24 hours.

value.error: Missing required fields: udid, host, reservedBy, duration
duration must be between 60000ms (1 minute) and 86400000ms (24 hours)

409.description: Reserved by someone else, or running an Appium session.

value.error: Device is already reserved by marco until 2026-10-04T15:00:00.000Z
Device is currently busy with an Appium session. Cannot reserve.

delete.description:
Ends the device's reservation at once. Only the user who took it,
or an admin, may: anyone else gets `403 not_reservation_holder`. A
reservation taken before 2.13 records no user, and anyone who may
reserve may still release it. A device outside the caller's teams
answers `404`.

`host` is URL-encoded (`http%3A%2F%2F192.168.1.100%3A4723`). The
device is the row of `udid` on that `host`; no such row answers
`404`.

Needs role `MEMBER` or above and the `devices` scope. Deprecated in
favour of leases.

403.description: The caller isn't the user who took the reservation, nor an admin; or lacks the role or scope.

value.message: Only the person who reserved this device, or an admin, can change the reservation.

post.summary: Extend a reservation
post.description:
Adds `duration` (at least 1 minute) to the current reservation's
end, keeping who holds it, its `reservedBy` and its reason. As with
a new reservation, it may end at most 24 hours from now. Only the
user who took it, or an admin, may extend it, as for releasing. A
device outside the caller's teams answers `404`.

`host` is URL-encoded, as for releasing. Needs role `MEMBER` or
above and the `devices` scope. Deprecated in favour of leases.

400.description: The device isn't reserved, or `duration` is invalid, under a minute, or would end the reservation more than 24 hours from now.

value.error: Invalid duration. Use: 1h, 2h, 4h, 8h or a number in milliseconds
duration must be at least 60000ms (1 minute)
A reservation can end at most 24 hours from now

403.description: The caller isn't the user who took the reservation, nor an admin; or lacks the role or scope.

value.message: Only the person who reserved this device, or an admin, can change the reservation.

post.summary: Lease a device
post.description:
Claims a free device that matches `filters` for `durationMs`, for a
programmatic client such as an SDK or MCP tool. The device is marked
busy, ports for the Appium driver are reserved on the server it is
attached to, and the answer carries `appiumCapabilities`: pass them
to `POST /session` unchanged. They include `xe:options.leaseId` and
`xe:options.leaseToken`, which prove the session holds the lease.

`leaseToken` is shown only in this answer and is never stored in
clear. Keep it: heartbeat, extend and release need it in the
`x-xenon-lease-token` header.

The lease ends after three missed heartbeats (every
`heartbeatSeconds`) or at `expiresAt`, whichever comes first; a
sweep runs every 30 s. Ending it frees the device unless a session
still holds it.

Matching: among the shared pool and the caller's teams (an admin is
unscoped), the devices that match every filter. `filters.platform`
is lowercase. `udid`, `deviceType`, `tags` (all must be present),
`platformVersion` (or `sdk`, the same thing), `minSDK`, `maxSDK`
and `deviceName` (the device's name, ignoring case) narrow it.
`404` means no device visible to you matches. Of those that match,
the lease takes one that is free, online, not already leased, not
blocked, not reserved, and not failing its health check, as a new
session would; `409` means some match but none of them is. Through
2.12 `sdk` and `deviceName` were ignored, blocked, reserved and
unhealthy devices could be leased, and `404` or `409` depended on
the platform alone.

Needs role `MEMBER` or above and the `devices` scope.

201.description: The lease. Keep `leaseToken`; it is not shown again.

400.description: `filters.platform` is missing.

404.description: No device the caller can see matches the filters.

409.description: Devices match, but none is free: busy, leased, blocked, reserved or unhealthy. Retry after `retryAfterMs`.

500.description: The lease could not be recorded.

example.message: Unique constraint failed on the fields

503.description:
A device was found but its ports could not be reserved: its server
didn't answer, or this server has no credentials for it
(`XENON_HUB_ACCESS_KEY` and `XENON_HUB_TOKEN`, needed whenever auth
is enabled). The device is freed again.

post.summary: Keep a lease alive
post.description:
Records a heartbeat, so the lease isn't ended for missed heartbeats.
It does not move `expiresAt`; use extend for that. Needs the lease
token in `x-xenon-lease-token`, role `MEMBER` or above and the
`devices` scope.

An unknown id answers like a wrong token (`403 token_mismatch`), so
lease ids can't be probed. A lease that has ended or passed
`expiresAt` answers `410` to its token's holder.

410.description: The lease has ended (released, expired or swept).

post.summary: Extend a lease
post.description:
Sets the lease to end `durationMs` from now (not from its current
end), and counts as a heartbeat. A lease never runs past 24 hours
after it was created: a later end is cut to that. A smaller
`durationMs` than the time left shortens the lease.

Needs the lease token in `x-xenon-lease-token`, role `MEMBER` or
above and the `devices` scope. An unknown id answers `403
token_mismatch`; an ended or expired lease answers `410`.

durationMs.description: How long from now the lease should last, in milliseconds.

400.description: `durationMs` is missing or not a number.

410.description: The lease has ended (released, expired or swept).

delete.description:
Ends the lease and gives back its ports. The device is freed unless
an Appium session still holds it; that session keeps it until it
ends. A lease past `expiresAt` that the sweep hasn't ended yet can
still be released.

Needs the lease token in `x-xenon-lease-token`, role `MEMBER` or
above and the `devices` scope. An unknown id answers `403
token_mismatch`; a lease that has already ended answers `404`.

204.description: The lease is released. No body.

get.summary: Get the version and features for SDKs
get.description:
The plugin's version and the SDK features this server supports, so
a client can check compatibility before leasing. Needs role
`MEMBER` or above.

post.summary: Reserve driver ports on this server
post.description:
Picks a free local port on this server for each purpose and records
it as leased to `udid` for `durationMs` plus 5 minutes. A hub calls
it on the server a device is attached to (itself included) when it
creates a lease, with its node credentials. The device isn't
checked to exist.

Needs role `ADMIN` and the `devices` scope.

durationMs.description: How long to hold the ports. Default 1800000 (30 minutes); a value of 0 or less uses the default.

leaseId.description: The lease the ports are for, if known.

200.description: The port reserved for each purpose.

400.description: `udid`, `host` or `purposes` is missing, or a purpose is unknown.

500.description: A port could not be reserved; none of this request's ports are kept.

example.details: Unique constraint failed on the fields (`port`)

get.summary: List the session requests waiting for a device
get.description:
The session requests waiting for a free device, as the
capabilities each client sent (`alwaysMatch` merged over the first
`firstMatch`), with `capability_id` and `createdAt`.

An admin sees all of them. A member sees a request that names
(`appium:udid`) a device they can see, or that they made, or that
came from one of their teams; the rest are only counted, in
`otherCount` of `GET /api/queue/summary`. A request queued by a
server that didn't record who made it is only counted for a
member.

Credentials are removed before a request is queued; any
secret-named key a row still holds reads `***REDACTED***`, for
every caller. Needs role `MEMBER` or above.

200.description: The waiting requests the caller may see, oldest first as stored.

get.summary: Count the session requests waiting
get.description:
How many session requests are waiting in the whole queue, as a bare
number. Every caller gets the same number, including requests they
can't see in `GET /api/queue`; it equals `total` in the summary.
Needs role `MEMBER` or above.

get.summary: Summarise the session queue
get.description:
Counts only. `total` and `byPlatform` cover the whole queue, as
`GET /api/queue/length` does; `otherCount` is how many of them the
caller doesn't get in detail from `GET /api/queue` (0 for an admin).
`avgDurationMs` is the average of the platform's last 20 finished
sessions, or 300000 (5 minutes) without history. Platforms are
lowercase; a request naming none is `any`. Needs role `MEMBER` or
above.

get.summary: Get a waiting request's position and wait
get.description:
Where one waiting session request stands among the requests for
its platform, and a rough wait: its position divided by the number
of devices of that platform, times the average session duration
(0 when it is first and a device is free).

`404` when the request has already been given a device, was
dropped, or is one the caller can't see in `GET /api/queue`: the
same answer as for an unknown id. Needs role `MEMBER` or above.

parameters.name: capability_id
parameters.description: The request's `capability_id`, as `GET /api/queue` lists it.

200.description: The request's place in the queue.

totalInQueue.description: Waiting requests for this platform (or any platform).

404.description: No such waiting request, or one the caller can't see.

post.summary: Report a node's devices to its hub
post.description:
How a node keeps its hub's device list current. Nodes call it
themselves, with the access key and token they were provisioned
with (`XENON_HUB_ACCESS_KEY`, `XENON_HUB_TOKEN`); it isn't meant for
other clients. Needs role `ADMIN` and the `devices` scope.

`type` selects the operation:

| `type` | Body | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `add` | the node's devices | Adds or refreshes each one |
| `remove` | devices, each with `udid` and `nodeId` or `host` | Forgets those devices |
| `unregister` | `[]` | Forgets every device of the node named by `nodeId` or `host` in the query |

A report (`add`) updates only what the node observes: discovery
fields such as name, version and ports, and health. Whether the
device is busy on the node goes to `nodeBusy`, and a preview hold
there to `nodeHold`. The hub's own settings (team, tags,
reservation, block, its claim for a session) are never taken from
a report, and a report of "free" never frees a device the hub has
claimed.

A removal takes only the node's own rows: by `nodeId` when given,
otherwise by exactly `host`. It never takes one of the hub's own
devices, and an entry with no udid, or with neither `nodeId` nor
`host`, takes nothing. Any other `type`, or none, changes nothing
and still answers `200`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The operation.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: For `unregister`, the node's host, used when `nodeId` isn't sent.

parameters.name: nodeId
parameters.description: For `unregister`, the node's id; every device the node reported goes, whatever its host.

200.description: The report was applied (or ignored, for an unknown `type`).

get.summary: List the hosts that have devices
get.description:
The distinct `host` of every device the caller can see: this
server and, on a hub, each node. A host whose devices all belong to
teams the caller isn't in isn't listed. Needs role `MEMBER` or
above.

get.summary: List the devices attached to this server
get.description:
Runs device discovery on this server now (Android and iOS, real
devices and emulators or simulators) and lists what it finds, with
each device's `state` as discovery reports it. Devices of other
servers aren't included. Needs role `ADMIN` and the `admin` scope.

get.summary: List the devices attached to one server
get.description:
When `host` is this server's bind address (`bindHostOrIp`), the
same as `GET /api/node/status`. Otherwise the hub looks for a
device whose host contains `host` and asks that server's
`/xenon/api/node/status`, returning its answer. That request
carries no credentials, so it works only against a node with auth
disabled; a node that refuses it, or can't be reached, answers
`502`.

Needs role `ADMIN` and the `admin` scope.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: This server's bind address, or part of a node's host (such as its IP).

404.description: No device is listed under that host, so there is nowhere to ask. Plain text.

text/html.example: Host 192.168.1.200 does not have any devices listed in database. I don't know how to forward request to that host

502.description: The node refused the request or couldn't be reached.

example.message: Could not get http://192.168.1.200:4723's status: connect ECONNREFUSED 192.168.1.200:4723

get.summary: Say whether a session exists on this node
get.description:
Node only: a hub asks it about each session it routes to the node,
about every 30 s, instead of sending a WebDriver command, which
would keep an abandoned session alive. It runs no command. Only a
server started with `hub` set has this route.

It is answered before the login, with what a command to that
session would need. With per-command auth off
(`XENON_REQUIRE_COMMAND_AUTH`) or auth disabled, no credential.
With it on, the hub's session token for that session in
`x-xenon-hub-token`; any other caller gets WebDriver's
unknown-session answer, `404`, and a hub key set that can't be
fetched is `503`. It isn't rate-limited.

Every answer from a node carries `x-xenon-node-sessions: 1`, so a
hub can tell a node that has the route from an older one.

200.description: Whether this node's Appium has the session.

get.summary: Collect a session's CPU and memory from this node
get.description:
Node only: a hub collects the CPU and memory samples a node has
taken for a session on one of its phones, every 10 s and once more
when the session ends. The node keeps them in memory: the newest
900 per session, an ended session's for 10 minutes. Only a server
started with `hub` set has this route.

`after` asks for the samples newer than that time, and the node
drops the older ones, so a later call never returns them again.
`state` is `sampling`, `stopped` (the sampler gave up), `ended`, or
`off` (the node has nothing for this session).

It is answered before the login, with the same rule as
`GET /api/node/sessions/{sessionId}`: no credential with
per-command auth off or auth disabled, otherwise the hub's session
token for that session. Every answer from a node carries
`x-xenon-node-metrics: 1`. It isn't rate-limited.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Epoch milliseconds; only newer samples are returned, and older ones are dropped. Anything that isn't a plain number is ignored.

get.summary: Check that the server answers
get.description:
A signed-in liveness check. `version` comes from the npm
environment, so a server not started through an npm script reports
`unknown (not running from npm package)`; `GET /api/ping` reports
the plugin's version. Needs role `MEMBER` or above.

get.summary: Get this server's WebDriver base path
get.description:
Where this server's Appium WebDriver API lives, relative to its
origin: `''` for Appium's default, or a path such as `/wd/hub`. A
hub asks each node before it sends the node a session or a command
(and caches the answer for a minute), since hub and node needn't
share a base path. Public: no credential and no rate limit.

basePath.description: Empty, or a path starting with `/` and without a trailing `/`.

get.summary: Get what the sign-in page may offer
get.description:
Public. Tells the sign-in page how a user who forgot their password can get back in, before
anyone is signed in.

`passwordReset` is `email` when the server has SMTP configured and `XENON_PUBLIC_URL` set to
its address (the forgot-password form really emails a link, which points there),
otherwise `admin` (the user must ask an administrator, who issues a link with
`POST /api/users/{id}/reset-link`). Nothing else about the mail setup is revealed.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
post.description:
Public. Checks the email (case-insensitive) and password of an `ACTIVE` user and, on success,
sets the `xenon_dashboard_session` cookie (HttpOnly, `SameSite=Strict`, `Secure` when the
request came over HTTPS or with `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`). The cookie lives for the
server's user-session lifetime (24 hours by default, `XENON_USER_SESSION_TTL_MS`, which may be
longer or shorter) and is renewed for that long on every authenticated request. Updates the user's last sign-in time.

A wrong password, an unknown email and an inactive user all answer the same `401`.

**Rate limit.** Each client IP (the first `X-Forwarded-For` address, else the socket address)
gets 5 attempts per 5 minutes by default, counting successful ones; a successful sign-in resets
the count. Past that the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`.

**Same-origin rule.** Like every state-changing request without an `x-xenon-access-key`
header, this needs an `Origin` or `Referer` from the same host (or one listed in
`XENON_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`), even though it carries no cookie yet. Without one it answers `403`.

204.description: Signed in. The session cookie is in `Set-Cookie`.

400.description: `email` or `password` is missing.

401.description: The email, password or account status is wrong.

post.summary: Sign out of the dashboard
post.description:
Public. Revokes the dashboard session named by the `xenon_dashboard_session` cookie, if the
request carries one, and clears the cookie. Always answers `204`, signed in or not.

Needs a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`, like every state-changing request without an
`x-xenon-access-key` header.

204.description: Signed out; the cookie is cleared.

post.summary: Email a password-reset link
post.description:
Public. Answers `204` at once, whatever the email, so it can't be used to find out which
addresses have accounts. Then, in the background, if the email belongs to an `ACTIVE` user and
the server can deliver mail (SMTP configured, or the opt-in log fallback
`XENON_PASSWORD_RESET_LOG_FALLBACK=true`), it creates a single-use reset token (valid 1 hour by
default, `XENON_RESET_TOKEN_TTL_MS`) and sends a link to
`<server address>/xenon/reset-password#<token>`. The server address is `XENON_PUBLIC_URL`
(such as `https://xenon.example.com`; a trailing `/xenon/` is dropped), never the request's
`Host`, which whoever asks chooses. Without a way to deliver mail, or without a usable
`XENON_PUBLIC_URL`, no token is created; `GET /api/auth/options` says `admin` then.

**Rate limit.** 3 requests per 15 minutes per client IP by default, then `429` with
`Retry-After`.

Needs a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`, like every state-changing request without an
`x-xenon-access-key` header.

204.description: Accepted. Sent whether or not a link was emailed.

post.summary: Check a password-reset token
post.description:
Public. Says whether a reset token from a reset link is still usable (exists, not used, not
expired, not revoked), so the reset page can show the form or an error. Doesn't use the token
up. The token goes in the body rather than the URL so it never reaches the request log.

Needs a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`, like every state-changing request without an
`x-xenon-access-key` header.

token.description: The token from the reset link.

post.summary: Set a new password with a reset token
post.description:
Public. Sets the user's password from a reset link's token. On success the token is used up,
every other outstanding reset link for that user is revoked, and every dashboard session of
that user is signed out. API tokens are not affected.

Needs a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`, like every state-changing request without an
`x-xenon-access-key` header.

400.description: A field is missing, or the password is shorter than 8 characters.

value.error: password must be at least 8 characters

get.summary: Get the server's public signing keys
get.description:
Public. The JSON Web Key Set that verifies the RS256 tokens this server signs: bearer tokens
from `POST /api/auth/token`, session tokens, and the hub tokens a hub sends its nodes. Nodes
fetch it from their hub. Answers `{ "keys": [] }` if the signing key hasn't been set up.

get.summary: Get who you are signed in as
get.description:
Who the credential belongs to: the user, their role, the scopes this credential carries, the
team the credential is bound to (`teamId`, API keys and bearer tokens only) and the user's
teams. `kind` says how the request authenticated: `user-session` (the dashboard cookie),
`api-key` (the key pair, or a raw API key in the cookie), or `bearer`.

`teams` lists the caller's teams by name; it is empty for admins, who see every team's
devices. With authentication disabled on the server the answer is a fixed synthetic
`SUPER_ADMIN` identity with `authDisabled: true` and no access key.

post.summary: Change your own password
post.description:
Changes the caller's password after checking the current one. Any signed-in user may call it.

Side effects: every outstanding password-reset link of the user is revoked, and, when the
request was made with the dashboard cookie, every other dashboard session of the user is
signed out (the current one stays). Made with an API key or bearer token, other dashboard
sessions stay signed in. API tokens are never affected.

A wrong current password answers `400`, not `401`. With authentication disabled there is no
real user and the answer is `400` (`user not found`). Cookie callers need a same-host
`Origin` or `Referer`.

400.description: A field is missing, the new password is too short, or the current password is wrong.

value.error: password must be at least 8 characters

post.summary: Mint a short-lived signed token
post.description:
Mints an RS256 JWT for the caller, signed by this server and verifiable with
`/api/auth/jwks.json`. Any signed-in user may call it.

- `audience: xenon-rest` (the default): a bearer token for this REST API, valid 1 hour. It
  carries the caller's role, the scopes of the credential used to mint it and its bound team.
- `audience: xenon-mcp`: a token for an MCP gateway, valid 24 hours by default
  (`XENON_MCP_TOKEN_TTL_SEC`). It carries granular `scopes` (by default `appium:use` and
  `xenon:devices:read`, as far as the caller's scopes allow) and, as a REST bearer token, only
  the flat scopes those need (`appium:use` gives `sessions`, `xenon:devices:lock` gives
  `devices`). When the grant includes `appium:use` the answer also has a `sessionToken`
  (audience `xenon-session`, same lifetime) to put in an Appium session's
  `xe:options.sessionToken`. It carries the `sessions` scope, and `admin` only when the
  credential minting it has `admin` and the grant is the default one (no `scopes` asked for) or
  a full-admin one. With `admin` a session may use a lease someone else made, and only while
  its user is still an `ADMIN` (a `SUPER_ADMIN`'s session may, `admin` or not). A credential
  without `sessions` or `admin`, a read-only one for instance, gets no `sessionToken`.

**Never longer than the credential.** A token minted with a Bearer token, or with an API key
that expires, ends no later than that credential: `expiresIn` is cut to what is left of it. A
credential with no time left answers `400`. A dashboard sign-in renews itself, so its tokens get
the full lifetime.

**Scopes follow the role.** A token's scopes are fixed when it is minted, but its `admin` scope
stops counting once its user is a `MEMBER`: the API and per-command auth read the token's scopes
without it.

Granular scopes a credential may grant: `read` gives `xenon:devices:read` and
`xenon:analytics:read`; `sessions` gives `appium:use` and `xenon:recordings`; `devices` gives
`xenon:devices:read`, `xenon:devices:lock` and `xenon:recordings`; `admin` gives all of them.

Cookie callers need a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

mcp.summary: An MCP token with chosen scopes

400.description:
An unsupported audience, `scopes` that isn't an array, an unknown granular scope, or a
credential with no time left to give the token.

value.details: the credential used to mint this token has expired

403.description:
An MCP scope the caller's credential can't grant (`scope_exceeds_key`), or the same-origin
check failed.

value.details: requested scope(s) exceed this key's grant: xenon:devices:lock

value.error: CSRF: Origin or Referer header required

post.summary: Turn a super-admin API token into a dashboard cookie
post.description:
Legacy. Puts a raw API token in the `xenon_dashboard_session` cookie (HttpOnly,
`SameSite=Strict`, same lifetime as a sign-in session), so a browser can use the dashboard as
that token. The request itself must already be authenticated, and the token in the body must
be a live API token whose owner is a `SUPER_ADMIN`. The cookie then authenticates with that
token's own scopes and team. Prefer `POST /api/auth/login`.

Cookie callers need a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

apiKey.description: A raw API token (the value shown once when it was created).

400.description: `apiKey` is missing.

401.description: No valid credential on the request, or the token in the body is unknown, revoked or expired.

403.description: The token's owner isn't a `SUPER_ADMIN`, or the same-origin check failed.

example.error: super-admin scope required for dashboard-session exchange

get.summary: Get your access key
get.description:
The caller's access key (`xen_…`), sent as `x-xenon-access-key` together with one of their API
tokens. Any signed-in user may call it. With authentication disabled it answers for the first
`SUPER_ADMIN` account.

post.summary: Rotate your access key
post.description:
Gives the caller a new access key. The old one stops working at once, for every one of their
API tokens: scripts and CI using the key pair must be updated. The tokens themselves are kept.

Since that cuts off every key pair the user has, whatever its scopes, it takes a dashboard
sign-in (the cookie) or a credential with the `admin` scope. Any other API token or Bearer
token, a `read`-only one for instance, gets `403`. Through 2.14 any credential could. With
authentication disabled it rotates the first `SUPER_ADMIN`'s key. Cookie callers need a
same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

403.description: A credential other than a dashboard sign-in, without the `admin` scope.

example.error: rotating the access key needs a dashboard sign-in or a credential with the admin scope

get.summary: List your API tokens

post.summary: Create an API token for yourself
post.description:
Creates an API token owned by the caller and returns its value **once**. Use it as
`x-xenon-token` with your access key.

`scopes` (some of `read`, `sessions`, `devices`, `admin`) may go beyond neither what the
caller's role allows nor the scopes of the credential making the request. The role allows:
`MEMBER`, `sessions` and `read`; `ADMIN`, `devices`, `sessions` and `read`; `SUPER_ADMIN`,
anything, `admin` included, or any narrower set. Without `scopes`, the token gets all of the
role's allowance, so a credential with fewer scopes must name them. Through 2.12 only the
role was checked, so an admin's `read`-only key could mint a wider token. The token has the
default rate limit (300 a minute) and no team binding.

Made with a credential that expires (a Bearer token, or an API key with an `expiresAt`), the
token expires no later than it: without `expiresAt` it gets that credential's, and a later
`expiresAt` answers `400`. Through 2.14 a 1-hour Bearer token could make a token that never
expired. From the dashboard, `expiresAt` may be left out for a token that never expires.

Any signed-in user may call it. Cookie callers need a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

400.description: `name` is missing, `expiresAt` is invalid, past or later than the credential you are using, a scope is unknown, or a scope is beyond your role or the credential you are using.

value.error: expiresAt must be in the future
expiresAt can be no later than the credential you are using, which expires at 2026-10-04T13:00:00.000Z
scopes must be some of read, sessions, devices, admin
cannot widen scopes beyond your role or the credential you are using

delete.summary: Revoke one of your API tokens
delete.description:
Revokes one of the caller's own API tokens; requests made with it are refused from then on.
A token of another user answers `404`, as an unknown one does. Revoking an already revoked
token of your own answers `204` again. Any signed-in user may call it. Cookie callers need a
same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The token's id.

404.description: No token of yours has this id.

get.summary: List user accounts
get.description:
Needs role `ADMIN` or above. A `SUPER_ADMIN` sees every account; an `ADMIN` sees only
`MEMBER` accounts. Oldest first.

Every `/api/users` request also needs the `admin` scope, as `/api/apikeys` and `/api/teams`
do: an admin's `read`-only key or token can't manage accounts. Through 2.12 it could.

post.summary: Create a user account
post.description:
Needs role `ADMIN` or above. An `ADMIN` may create only `MEMBER` accounts; a `SUPER_ADMIN` any
role. The email is stored lower-case. The account is `ACTIVE` and gets its own access key.

Without `password` the server generates a 12-character temporary password and returns it once
as `temporaryPassword`; with one, it isn't echoed back. Cookie callers need a same-host
`Origin` or `Referer`.

400.description: A field is missing, the role is unknown, or the password is shorter than 8 characters.

value.error: role must be SUPER_ADMIN | ADMIN | MEMBER
password must be at least 8 characters

403.description: Your role is below `ADMIN`, or you may not create an account with that role.

example.error: cannot create user with role ADMIN

409.description: An account with this email already exists.

patch.summary: Change a user's name, role or status
patch.description:
Needs role `ADMIN` or above. An `ADMIN` may change only `MEMBER` accounts and may not promote
anyone above `MEMBER`; a `SUPER_ADMIN` may change anyone. Only the fields sent are changed; the
email can't be changed.

- You can't change your own role.
- The last active `SUPER_ADMIN` can't be demoted or deactivated.
- Setting `status` to `INACTIVE` signs the user out of every dashboard session. Their API
  tokens, bearer tokens and session tokens stop working too, since an inactive user's
  credentials are refused: on this API at once, for a new Appium session at once, and for the
  commands of a session already running within 30 seconds with `XENON_REQUIRE_COMMAND_AUTH`.

Cookie callers need a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

200.description: The account as it now is.

400.description: Your own role, an unknown role, or the last active super-admin.

value.error: cannot role-change yourself; use a different super-admin to manage your own account
cannot remove or demote the last active super-admin; promote another user first

403.description: Your role is below `ADMIN`, or too low for this account or the new role.

delete.description:
Needs role `ADMIN` or above. An `ADMIN` may delete only `MEMBER` accounts. Deletes the account,
its dashboard sessions, its API tokens and its team memberships. You can't delete yourself, and
the last active `SUPER_ADMIN` can't be deleted. Cookie callers need a same-host `Origin` or
`Referer`.

400.description: Yourself, or the last active super-admin.

example.error: cannot delete yourself; use a different super-admin to manage your own account

403.description: Your role is below `ADMIN`, or too low for this account.

post.summary: Issue a password-reset link for a user
post.description:
Needs role `ADMIN` or above. An `ADMIN` may issue links only for `MEMBER` accounts. Creates a
single-use reset link for an `ACTIVE` user, valid 1 hour by default.

With SMTP and `XENON_PUBLIC_URL` configured the link is emailed to the user and the answer is
`emailed: true`; the emailed link points at `XENON_PUBLIC_URL`, never at the request's `Host`.
Without either the link is returned once, in this answer only (`Cache-Control: no-store`), for
the admin to pass on; it is never written to the server log. A returned link points at
`XENON_PUBLIC_URL` when it is set, else at the address the admin reached the server on. Your own password goes through
`POST /api/auth/change-password` instead. Cookie callers need a same-host `Origin` or
`Referer`.

200.description: The link was emailed, or here it is.

400.description: The account is your own.

example.error: cannot issue a reset link for yourself; use a different super-admin to manage your own account

403.description: Your role is below `ADMIN`, or too low for this account.

get.summary: List the teams
get.description:
Every team, oldest first, with how many devices and members each has. Needs role `ADMIN` or
above and the `admin` scope.

post.summary: Create a team
post.description:
Creates a team. The name is trimmed and must be unique. Needs role `ADMIN` or above and the
`admin` scope. Cookie callers need a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

400.description: `name` is missing or blank.

409.description: A team with this name exists.

delete.description:
Deletes a team that owns no devices, has no members and owns no apps; otherwise it refuses with
`400` and says what is left, so nothing is quietly moved to the shared pool. Any API key still
bound to the team is unbound. An unknown id also answers `400`. Needs role `ADMIN` or above and
the `admin` scope. Cookie callers need a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

400.description: The team still owns devices, members or apps, or doesn't exist.

example.error: Team still has 2 device(s), 3 member(s) and 0 app(s). Reassign them before deleting.

get.summary: List a team's members
get.description:
The users in a team, in the order they were added. An unknown team answers an empty list.
Needs role `ADMIN` or above and the `admin` scope.

post.summary: Add a user to a team
post.description:
Adds a user to a team. The user then sees the team's devices, apps and sessions from their next
request (live dashboard events from their next reconnect). Needs role `ADMIN` or above and the
`admin` scope. An unknown team or user, or a user already in the team, answers `400` with the
database's message. Cookie callers need a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

400.description: `userId` is missing, or the user or team is unknown, or the user is already a member.

delete.summary: Remove a user from a team
delete.description:
Takes a user out of a team. The user's account and API tokens are kept. A user who isn't in the
team answers `400`. Needs role `ADMIN` or above and the `admin` scope. Cookie callers need a
same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The user's id.

400.description: The user isn't a member of this team.

example.error: An operation failed because it depends on one or more records that were required but not found.

get.summary: List the lab's API keys
get.description:
Every API token in the lab that hasn't been revoked, whoever owns it, newest first, expired ones
included. The token values are never returned. Needs role `ADMIN` or above and the `admin`
scope.

post.summary: Create an API key
post.description:
Creates an API token owned by the caller and returns its value **once** as `key`; it is used as
`x-xenon-token` with the caller's access key. Unlike `POST /api/profile/tokens`, it can name a
team, set its rate limit and grant any scope, `admin` included. `scopes` must be some of `read`,
`sessions`, `devices` and `admin`; any other string answers `400` (through 2.14 it was stored,
and gave the key nothing). Needs role `ADMIN` or above and the `admin` scope. Cookie callers
need a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

**The team doesn't narrow the key.** The key belongs to the caller, an administrator, and an
administrator's credentials reach every team's devices, so the key does too whichever team it
names. The team is recorded on the leases the key takes, and limits the key only if its owner
is later made a `MEMBER`. A test session keeps to one team with `xe:options.team`.

Made with a credential that expires (a Bearer token, or an API key with an `expiresAt`), the
key expires no later than it: without `expiresAt` it gets that credential's, and a later
`expiresAt` answers `400`.

key.description: The token value. Shown only now.

400.description: `name` or `scopes` is missing, a scope is unknown, or `expiresAt` is invalid, past or later than the credential making the request.

value.error: scopes must be some of read, sessions, devices, admin
expiresAt must be an ISO-8601 datetime

delete.description:
Revokes any API token in the lab, whoever owns it. Requests made with it are refused from then
on; the row is kept, marked revoked. Needs role `ADMIN` or above and the `admin` scope. Cookie
callers need a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

An unknown id answers `404`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The key's id.

get.summary: List projects
get.description:
The projects the caller may see: a member sees their teams' projects and the shared ones
(no team); an admin sees all. Any signed-in user may call it.

post.summary: Create a project
post.description:
Creates a project, optionally owned by a team (`teamId`, null or blank for shared). The name is
trimmed. Needs the `admin` scope; no role is checked beyond that. Cookie callers need a
same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

teamId.description: The owning team. Not checked against existing teams.

400.description: `name` is missing or blank.

post.summary: Send in a batch of MCP audit events
post.description:
For an MCP gateway: records a batch of tool-call audit events in the server's event log
(type `mcp_audit`), tagged with the credential's team. Needs the `admin` scope (any role). The
whole batch is checked first: one bad event refuses all of it. At most 1000 events per batch.
Answers `202` with the count; writes happen in the background and a failed write is dropped.
Cookie callers need a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

400.description: `events` is not an array, is longer than 1000, or an event is invalid.

get.summary: Get the server's version and features
get.description:
Feature detection for SDKs and tools: the server's version and which features it has. Most are
always `true` in this version; `sessionTokenGate` (`XENON_REQUIRE_SESSION_TOKEN`) and
`commandAuth` (`XENON_REQUIRE_COMMAND_AUTH`) report the live settings. Any signed-in user may
call it.

get.summary: Check that the server is up
get.description:
Liveness probe. Public: no credential, no rate limit. Answers `{ "ok": true }` as soon as
the API is serving requests. It checks nothing else (not the database, not the devices),
so use it for load-balancer and Kubernetes liveness checks, not readiness.

get.summary: Check a credential and read the server version
get.description:
Answers `{ pong, version }` for any valid credential. Use it to confirm that a key pair,
bearer token or dashboard session is accepted, and to read the running Xenon version.
Counts against the `read` rate-limit budget.

get.summary: Read server metrics in Prometheus format
get.description:
Prometheus text exposition of the server's counters and gauges. Any valid credential may
read it (no role or scope beyond being signed in); point a scraper at it with a key pair
or bearer token.

Series:
- `xenon_sessions_total{status="started"|"success"|"failure"}`: persisted session counters.
- `xenon_sessions_active`: sessions this server tracks right now.
- `xenon_devices_total`, `xenon_devices_busy`, `xenon_devices_offline`.
- `xenon_healing_total{status="attempt"|"success"}`: persisted self-healing counters.
- Per-tier healing series (`xenon_heal_tier_attempts_total`, `..._successes_total`,
  `..._failures_total`, `xenon_heal_tier_duration_seconds_sum`, labelled `tier` and
  `name`), `xenon_heal_all_tiers_failed_total` and
  `xenon_heal_tier_skipped_remaining_total`. These are kept in memory and start again
  from zero when the server restarts.

text/plain.example:
# HELP xenon_sessions_total Total number of sessions across all time
# TYPE xenon_sessions_total counter
xenon_sessions_total{status="started"} 1284
xenon_sessions_total{status="success"} 1190
xenon_sessions_total{status="failure"} 94
# HELP xenon_sessions_active Current active sessions in the hub
# TYPE xenon_sessions_active gauge
xenon_sessions_active 3
# HELP xenon_devices_total Total managed devices in the fleet
# TYPE xenon_devices_total gauge
xenon_devices_total 12

get.summary: Read the Appium arguments the server stored
get.description:
The plugin arguments this lab has stored, one object per stored entry, oldest first. They
include the database URL, AI and cloud provider settings and the hub URL, so this needs
the `ADMIN` role and the `admin` scope. Values are redacted the way the server log
redacts them: a value under a key that looks secret (password, token, API key, auth,
database URL, and similar) and any string shaped like a provider key reads
`***REDACTED***`.

get.summary: List the child processes Xenon supervises
get.description:
A snapshot of the long-lived child processes this server has started and tracks:
WebDriverAgent, ffmpeg recorders, `adb reverse` forwards, iOS MJPEG forwarders, log
tailers and others. Useful when a host runs hot or a device seems wedged. `sessionId` and
`udid` are present only when the process belongs to one. Needs the `ADMIN` role and the
`admin` scope.

get.summary: Read the lab's settings and AI provider
get.description:
The lab-wide settings in effect (health checks, build cleanup and the AI self-healing
switch), merged with the AI settings in effect (provider, models and base URL). Each
setting is the value saved in the dashboard, else the plugin option or environment
variable the server was started with, else the default, which is also what the server
runs with. A model or base URL set nowhere is absent: the provider's own applies. A user
name, password or query value in the base URL is sent as `***`. `defaults` holds the defaults themselves, which
is what "restore defaults" goes back to. Only `healthCheckSchedule` can be absent: no
schedule is set. Through 2.13 `enableSelfHealing` was neither stored nor sent, so the
Settings page always showed it on.
API keys are never returned: `geminiSet`, `openaiSet` and `anthropicSet` say only
whether one is configured. Needs the `ADMIN` role or above, as the dashboard's settings
pages do; through 2.12 any signed-in user could read it. Through 2.13 a setting never
saved was absent, and `defaults` was not sent.

500.description: The settings could not be read.

post.summary: Change the lab's settings and AI provider
post.description:
Saves the lab-wide settings and changes the AI provider settings. Every field is
optional; fields not sent are left as they are, and unknown fields are ignored.

- Health-check and build-cleanup fields are stored in the database. A stored value
  replaces the plugin option the server was started with, and applies without a
  restart: the health check within a minute, the retention values at the next cleanup
  run, and a new `buildCleanupSchedule` at once. The cleanup fields are checked first
  and refused with `400` when they could not work: `buildCleanupDays` and
  `buildCleanupMaxCount` must be whole numbers of at least 1, `buildCleanupSchedule` a
  cron expression of five or six fields, `deleteBuildAssets` true or false. Nothing is
  saved then. Send only the fields to change: a field sent is saved as the lab's own.
  Through 2.13 only one setting could be saved: saving a second failed with a `500`.
- `enableSelfHealing` (true or false; anything else is refused with `400`) is the AI
  self-healing switch. A stored value replaces the plugin option the server was started
  with, and applies to the next command this server runs, with no restart. A session's
  own `xe:options.healingTiers` still limits the tiers it may use. Through 2.13 the
  switch was accepted and ignored. The value belongs to the server it is saved on:
  saving it on a hub changes the hub's own sessions, not those on a node's phones,
  which the node's own setting decides.
- AI fields (`aiProvider`, `aiModel`, `aiBaseUrl` and the per-provider models) are stored
  too. A stored value replaces the plugin option or environment variable the server was
  started with, and applies to the next AI call, with no restart. An empty value removes
  the stored one, and the server's own applies again. They are checked first and refused
  with `400`: `aiProvider` must be `gemini`, `openai`, `anthropic` or `ollama`; a model
  name has no spaces and at most 200 characters; `aiBaseUrl` is an http or https address
  with no user name, password or query. Through 2.14 they changed the running server
  only, and a restart undid them. Like the self-healing switch, they belong to the server
  they are saved on.
- API keys can't be set here, and are never stored: they come from the server's
  environment. `aiTemperature`, `aiMaxTokens` and `aiTopP`, which the AI engine page sent
  through 2.14, were never used by any AI call and are ignored like any unknown field.

Needs the `SUPER_ADMIN` role and the `admin` scope; an `ADMIN` gets `403` with a message
saying so (through 2.12 an `ADMIN` could). With the dashboard cookie the request must
come from the same host (`Origin` or `Referer`).

400.description: A build-cleanup field, the self-healing switch or an AI field has a value that could not work. Nothing was saved.

example.message: buildCleanupDays must be a whole number of at least 1.

500.description: The settings could not be saved.

post.summary: Reset every device's healed-selector count
post.description:
Sets every device's healed-selector count (`totalHealedCount`) back to zero. Nothing else
is reset: the session and healing counters on `/api/metrics` are unchanged. Takes no
body. Needs the `SUPER_ADMIN` role and the `admin` scope, as every change under
`/api/config` does. With the dashboard cookie the request must come from the same host.

500.description: The counts could not be reset.

post.summary: Test a connection to an AI provider
post.description:
Sends a one-line prompt to an AI provider and says whether it answered. The provider,
model and base URL are taken from the body, falling back to the server's current
settings. The API key is the server's own (from its environment); a key in the body is
used only when the server has none for that provider. Nothing is saved.

The answer is `200` whether or not the connection worked: read `success`. A provider that
answers but is out of quota still counts as a success, with a note in `message`.

post.summary: Add a webhook
post.description:
Adds a webhook, active at once. When one of its `events` happens Xenon POSTs to `url`:

- with `payloadTemplate`: the template, with each `{{name}}` (or `{{a.b}}`, `{{list.0.b}}`)
  replaced from the event (`eventType` plus the event's fields, below). A template that
  is JSON as written is filled in string by string, so a value holding a quote or a line
  break can't break it, and is sent as that JSON. Any other template is filled in as
  text and sent as JSON if the result parses, otherwise as `{ "text": "<result>" }`. A
  `{{name}}` the event doesn't have is left as written;
- otherwise, `type: slack`: a Slack message with an attachment;
- otherwise: `{ "event": "<event>", "payload": { ... } }`.

Each delivery is one POST, never retried. A webhook that refuses an event or can't be
reached doesn't fail the event: the failure is logged on the server and the other
webhooks still get it. Use `POST /api/webhook/test` to see whether a webhook accepts
deliveries.

What each event carries (a device event also has the device's other fields, which may
change; only the names listed are promised):

- `device_offline`, `device_new`: `udid`, `name`, `host`, `platform`.
Sent when a device stops being reported, or is first detected.

- `session_failed`: `sessionId`, `sessionName`, `failureReason`, `udid`, `deviceName`,
`platform`, `osVersion`, `startTime`, `endTime` (ISO 8601; unknown values are empty
text). Sent once per session when it ends as failed: the test marked it failed, a command
failed, it timed out for inactivity, its driver crashed, or its heartbeat stopped. Not
when the server itself shuts down, not for a session already failed when the server
started, and not when the dashboard is off, since the session's record is what it is
built from.

- `selector_health_digest`: `windowDays`, `totalHeals`, `distinctSelectors` and
`hotspots`, a list of `healCount`, `originalSelector` and `suggestedRewrite`.

Neither `url` nor the event names are checked. Needs the `ADMIN` role and the `admin`
scope. With the dashboard cookie the request must come from the same host.

400.description: `url` or the `events` array is missing.

example.error: Invalid parameters: url and events array required

500.description: The webhook could not be saved.

cookie the request must come from the same host. An unknown id answers `404`.

Answers `200` when `url` accepted the delivery (a 2xx), and `502 delivery_failed`, with
the reason, when it refused it or couldn't be reached. Needs the `ADMIN` role and the
`admin` scope. With the dashboard cookie the request must come from the same host.

post.summary: Start recording one or more phones
post.description:
Starts one recording group: one video per phone and, for two or more phones, a
side-by-side composite video. The phone's live stream is started if it isn't running.
Each phone is held for the caller (as a live preview is) until the recording ends.

All or nothing up front: if any phone is busy, or the server's cap on simultaneous
recordings would be exceeded, nothing starts (`409`). A phone is busy when it is already
being recorded, held by another user, or running an Appium session. Your own preview hold
doesn't count. After that, a phone whose capture fails to start is left out of
`recordings` and the rest record on.

Members may record only phones they can see: if any is outside their teams, or unknown,
the answer is `404` and nothing starts. Any signed-in user whose credential has the `devices` scope (or `admin`) may call it.
With the dashboard cookie the request must come from the same host.

The recording groups still running that the caller holds a phone of, so the Live
devices page can pick them back up after a reload. A group is the caller's when they hold
the preview hold on any of its phones; admins get only their own too. Phones the caller
can't see are left out, with their marks. Only marks still on screen (not yet cleared)
are returned.

`startedAt` is the group's t=0, which mark timecodes count from. `serverNow` lets the
client correct for clock skew. Any signed-in user may call it.

marks, each sorted by timecode. Only the phones the caller can see are included; with
none, the answer is `404`. Any signed-in user may call it.

Deletes the recording's videos, bookmarks and marks, for the phones the caller can see.
A phone on another team stays, with the composite video, until no phone of the recording
is left; an admin sees every phone, so deletes the whole recording. Irreversible.

Only the person who started the recording, or an admin, may delete it (`403 not_owner`).
A recording any of whose phones is still recording can't be deleted (`409`). An API key
needs the `devices` scope (or `admin`). With the dashboard cookie the request must come
from the same host. The checks run in the order `404`, `409`, `403`.

Not the person who started it, or the credential lacks the `devices` scope, or a
browser request failed the same-origin check.

post.description:
Starts recording one more phone in an existing group. Its marks are placed on the group's
timeline by how late it joined. It doesn't join the side-by-side composite, which keeps
the phones it started with.

Like starting a recording, it is refused with `409` if the phone is busy or the server's
recording cap is reached, and nothing starts. A member gets `404` for a group they can't
see any phone of, or a phone outside their teams. Any signed-in user whose credential has the `devices` scope (or `admin`) may call it.
With the dashboard cookie the request must come from the same host.

example.error: udid must be a non-empty string

post.summary: Stop a recording
post.description:
Stops every phone of the group, the side-by-side composite first, and finishes each video
separately: a phone whose video fails doesn't stop the others. Each phone is then let go
(its preview hold released once nobody watches it).

Stopping is group-wide even for a caller who sees only some of its phones; the answer
lists only the phones they can see. Each video's `status` is `STOPPED`, or `FAILED` when
its file is missing or too small to play. `durationMs` is the video's own length.

A phone whose recording had already ended (its stream ended earlier, or the group was
already stopped) is left as it is: its end, length and failure reason are kept, and the
phone isn't let go a second time. It is reported with its stored `status`, `durationMs`
and `sizeBytes`, so stopping a group again changes none of its videos. A phone whose
stream is ending at that very moment is reported as it stands, and may still say
`RECORDING`.

A member gets `404` for a group they can't see any phone of. Any signed-in user whose credential has the `devices` scope (or `admin`) may call it.
With the dashboard cookie the request must come from the same host.

The recording must belong to this group and be on a phone the caller can see, otherwise
`404`. Dashboards watching the recording are told at once. Any signed-in user whose credential has the `devices` scope (or `admin`) may call it.
With the dashboard cookie the request must come from the same host.

timeline, on one phone's recording. It stays on screen until the marks are cleared
(`annotations/clear`), and is burned into the downloaded videos.

`geometry` is a JSON string with the mark's box in coordinates from 0 to 1 of the frame:
`{"x":…,"y":…,"w":…,"h":…}`. `image` is optional: the mark as the browser drew it, a PNG
data URL of at most 2 MiB decoded, burned in as drawn instead of the server's own drawing.

The recording must belong to this group and be on a phone the caller can see, otherwise
`404`. Dashboards watching the recording are told at once. Any signed-in user whose credential has the `devices` scope (or `admin`) may call it.
With the dashboard cookie the request must come from the same host.

it. Marks are kept (they show up to that point in the video), not deleted. Marks that
started later, or were already cleared, are left alone, so repeating a clear changes
nothing. Only the marks on phones the caller can see are cleared; an admin's clear covers
the whole group.

A member gets `404` for a group they can't see any phone of. Any signed-in user whose credential has the `devices` scope (or `admin`) may call it.

post.description:
Builds a zip for a session and streams it as a download. The zip holds `manifest.json` (session, device, capabilities, last command, the time window and any warnings), `README.md` and `logs.txt`, plus `video.mp4`, `network.har` and `ai-summary.txt` when the session has them. `network.har`, every request the app made with its headers and bodies, is added only for an `ADMIN` or `SUPER_ADMIN`, who may read it on `/api/interceptor`; for anyone else the manifest's warnings say it was left out. Through 2.12 every caller who could see the session got it.

- `mode=slice` covers only the last `windowSec` seconds of the session (5 to 600, default 60), video and logs included.
- `mode=full` covers the whole session; `windowSec` is ignored.

When the download finishes, dashboards that can see the session's device get a `bug report generated` live event. A session the caller may not see answers `404`, like an unknown one. Any signed-in user (role `MEMBER` or above) may call it. With the dashboard cookie, the request needs a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

parameters.description: The Appium session id.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: The last few seconds, or the whole session.

parameters.name: windowSec
parameters.description: With `mode=slice`, how many seconds before the session's end to cover.

200.description: The zip, as an attachment named `bugreport-<sessionId>-<generatedAt>.zip`.

400.description: `mode` is missing or unknown, or `windowSec` is out of range.

404.description: The session is unknown, or one the caller may not see.

500.description: The bundle couldn't be assembled.

get.summary: List builds
get.description: Lists builds, newest first, with their session counts by outcome. Builds are shared by name, so one build can hold several teams' sessions: a member sees a build only if at least one of its sessions is visible to them, and its counts cover those sessions only. An admin sees every build and every session. `success`, `passed` and `ended` count as passed; `failed`, `error` and `timeout` as failed. Any signed-in user (role `MEMBER` or above) may call it.

Give `sessionIds` to export only those sessions of the build.

A member gets only the sessions on devices of their teams or the shared pool; a session whose device no longer has a row is left out. post.summary: Mark a selector fixed, mute it or undo either
post.description:
Changes a selector's lab-wide status and records who did it (and, for a mute, why):
- `mark_fixed`: starts verification (status `pending`), resetting its clean-build count. Refused with `409` on a muted selector.
- `mute`: status `muted`. Muting again refreshes the time and records the new reason.
- `unmute`: back to `active`, or the status row is removed when the selector has no other history (`state: null`). On a selector that isn't muted it changes nothing and answers its current row.
- `cancel_verification`: undoes `mark_fixed` while it is `pending`; refused with `409` otherwise. The row is removed when there is no other history.

Dashboards are told of every change at once. Needs role `MEMBER` and the `sessions` scope (`admin` has it). The selector must have healed in a session the caller may see; otherwise `404`, as for an unknown one. With the dashboard cookie, the request needs a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

original_strategy.description: The strategy; may be empty for heals recorded with no strategy.

reason.description: Why it is muted. Kept for `mute` only, trimmed.

example.reason: Login screen is being redesigned; selector changes next sprint

200.description: The selector's stored status row after the change, or null when it was removed.

400.description: A field is missing, the action is unknown, or the reason is too long.

value.error: original_strategy, original_selector, and action are required
action must be one of mark_fixed, mute, unmute, cancel_verification
reason must be text of at most 500 characters

409.description: The action doesn't fit the selector's current status.

example.error: Cannot markFixed on a muted selector (accessibility id=login-btn)

500.description: The change couldn't be saved.

post.summary: Add a mock rule to a running session
post.description: Adds a mock rule to a session whose interceptor is running. A rule matches a request by URL (exact, or a glob where `*` is any text without `/` and `**` any text) and optionally by method, then rewrites the request, answers with `respondWith` without reaching the server, or changes the real response (`rewriteResponse`). When several rules match, the newest wins. Without an `id` one is generated. The body is stored as given and isn't validated, so send a `match.url`. Needs role `ADMIN`. With the dashboard cookie, the request needs a same-host `Origin` or `Referer`.

400.description: The rule couldn't be added.
